text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: kv-cache continuous-batching error rate spike (sev2) on prod-east-1 at 2026-03-15T09:02:25Z. Alert: 70% increase in 5xx for /v1/generate on qwen-mqa-32k.

kevin (oncall): seeing the same. p95 latency jumped from 220ms -> 2.1s, 5xxs mostly 503 from serving layer. tagging @maya and @sarah.

maya (runtime): got logs, looks like KV cache size per-shard exploded for requests hitting long-context Qwen MQA runs. continuous_batch window stacking a lot of prefixes -> memory pressure -> eviction storm -> timeouts.

sarah (models): Qwen MQA has heavier prefix KV growth (token-level meta) vs GQA. Did we roll any model-specific batching change?

kevin (oncall): no recent model config changes in last 24h besides a small autoscaling tweak for dedicated pools. verifying commit history now.

david (sre): metrics dump:
```
metric: kv_cache_entries_per_shard (prod-east-1)
- normal: 12k
- current: 182k
metric: cont_batch_window_active_requests
- normal: 40
- current: 650
error: eviction-write-failures increased x8
```

maya (runtime): root cause hypothesis: continuous batching combined with prefetch + MQA's internal key expansion is multiplying kv entries per request. When batch window grows, we are merging prefixes across sessions and keeping per-request KV longer than expected. This leaks across model variant because Qwen-MQA's internal caching of attention context includes extra metadata.

sarah (models): yeah, Qwen has a feature where MQA stores token span annotations in KV for rerankers — increases KV density. We should treat MQA variants as vulnerable to cont-batch expansion.

lisa (support): any customer impact? I see increased error rates for several high-throughput customers in prod-east-1, some pages to customers (enterprise) about degraded gen throughput.

kevin (oncall): assessed impacted customers: 3 enterprise customers with dedicated pools + 9 hosted customers saw elevated error rates. Notified account leads with preliminary incident note.

maya (runtime): mitigation plan (live):
1) reduce continuous_batch window from 150ms -> 50ms for prod-east-1 globally.
2) disable prefetch for MQA-tagged models (qwen-mqa variants) via runtime feature flag.
3) temporarily lower max_batch_size from 128 -> 32 for Qwen MQA routes.
4) enable aggressive KV TTL trimming: key_ttl_secs from 3600 -> 300 for affected shards.

kevin (oncall): executing 1 & 2 now. applying flag: `runtime.features.prefetch_mqa=false` to prod-east-1 via console.

maya (runtime): applying config change:
```
shardctl set-config --region prod-east-1 \
  --continuous-batch-window-ms 50 \
  --kv-default-ttl 300
```

pagerduty: Change executed by kevin at 2026-03-15T09:06:41Z.

david (sre): initial metrics after change (1m): cont_batch_active_requests dropped to ~90, kv entries per shard down to ~28k, 5xxs dropping. p95 latency trending down to 330ms.

sarah (models): confirming model-level disable: Qwen-MQA routes flagged. Might cause a small latency increase single-request but avoids eviction storms.

lisa (support): customers reporting immediate improvement, one still seeing errors on a small subset of endpoints. I'm following up with account team.

kevin (oncall): next steps: keep mitigation in place for 1 hour, monitor for regression. If stable, create a targeted config change to permanently mark MQA-class models with stricter prefetch/cont-batch defaults. Need engineering PR to make this policy-driven. @maya to own runtime change, @sarah for model tagging.

maya (runtime): will open runtime PR to:
- add model_class flag handling (gqa|mqa) at routing time
- default cont-batch window for mqa = 40ms, prefetch = false, max_batch_size = 32
Will include canary rollout to prod-east-1 then global.

sarah (models): will emit updated model metadata for qwen-mqa and other mqa variants so the runtime can pick them up. Also running a quick eval to measure token-density per request to tune TTL.

david (sre): recommend a follow-up hotfix to reduce the KV growth in codepath: garbage collect stale token-span metadata after response finalization (short-term) and longer-term refactor. I'll add a postmortem action.

kevin (oncall): escalation? any on-call need? looks contained but still in mitigation. If 5xxs don't drop below 2% in 20m -> escalate to infra leads.

maya (runtime): 10m post-change: stable. 5xxs for qwen-mqa down from 12% -> 1.3%. p95 for mixed traffic ~290ms.

lisa (support): notifying affected customers with update: "We applied temporary runtime throttles and config changes; service is stabilizing. We'll follow up with postmortem and ETA for permanent fix."

kevin (oncall): starting handoff notes for next oncall (maya taking over in 35m):
- Incident: KV cache blowup driven by continuous-batching + prefetch for MQA models (qwen-mqa primary).
- Actions taken: reduced cont-batch window to 50ms, disabled prefetch for MQA, lowered max_batch_size for Qwen MQA routes, reduced kv TTL to 300s.
- Current state: stable, 5xxs reduced to ~1.3%, p95 ~300ms.
- Outstanding: runtime PR to make model-class defaults permanent + model metadata updates, SRE hotfix for token-span GC, validation of changes across regions (prod-west-1 scheduled next).
- Customer impact: transient errors for 12 customers (3 enterprise, 9 hosted); all notified.
- Pager: no pages expected unless 5xx > 2% for next 20m.

maya (runtime): taking over monitoring. will start PR and canary plan. leaving a short TODO in thread for oncall next shift: if traffic increases, consider routing qwen-mqa traffic to ded-2 pool with reserved capacity as temporary mitigation.

kevin (oncall): thanks team. I'll post incident summary and open a postmortem ticket with action owners. handing off to maya now. :handshake:

maya (runtime): thanks, taking it. brief handoff: watch cont-batch active_requests, kv_entries_per_shard, eviction-writes. I'll update thread with PR link and rollout timeline.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to mitigated at 2026-03-15T09:22:55Z by kevin.

kevin (oncall): quick note for postmortem: include load-tests for MQA models with continuous batching enabled, add automated alert for kv_entries_per_shard crossing 50k, and bake model_class defaults into onboarding.

maya (runtime): noted. adding owners: runtime (maya/david), models (sarah), support (lisa). ending live mitigation portion; moving to post-incident cleanup.

lisa (support): I'll follow up with account teams and add customer impact doc to OTRS.

kevin (oncall): closing thread handoff.
